stop_status: CLEAR - no confirmed memory-safety defect remains. One Rust UB mechanism (unsynchronised process-global ASN.1 method registry), one unchecked allocation-arithmetic class in the parameter builder, three allocator-seam coordinate divergences, one builder-block size divergence, one false unsafe Sync marker and one incomplete RSA load contract were found and repaired. FAST, BATCH (serial and --test-threads=4) pass, and the new checked-arithmetic control fires on the pre-fix shape. Nothing is promoted to SAFETY_DISCHARGED or SAFE_COMPATIBLE.

authority.source: openssl-3.6.4 crypto/param_build.c (builder construction/free, definition push, conversion, secure/ordinary block allocation), crypto/http/http_client.c (REQ_CTX lifecycle, nbio state machine, open/exchange/get/transfer/close callback ownership), crypto/err/err.c + err_local.h + err_blocks.c + err_save.c (ERR_STATE ownership, slot buffers, queue reads, print callback), providers/implementations/keymgmt/rsa_kmgmt.c (object path, import/export, get_params, generation and load/dup), crypto/asn1/ameth_lib.c (application method registry, lookup, copy/free and engine arms), cross-checked line by line against the crate bodies.
authority.abi: C ABI unchanged: no export, signature, #[repr(C)] public handle or unsafe lint attribute changed. OSSL_PARAM_BLD is opaque; its block was reduced to the authority's three words and made #[repr(C)], with no change to any exported signature. The new std::sync::Mutex is private registry state.
external_contracts: OSSL_PARAM_BLD keys and pushed value pointers are borrowed and must outlive to_param; to_param consumes the recorded definitions and returns one CRYPTO_malloc block (plus one CRYPTO_secure_malloc block when a secure value was pushed) released by OSSL_PARAM_free.

A secure value is one allocated by the secure heap; the builder writes it into the secure block and never into the ordinary block. A caller-installed allocator hook sees the authority's block extents or a refusal.

OSSL_HTTP_REQ_CTX owns its memory BIO, buffer, duplicated proxy/server/port/expected_ct strings and (when free_wbio is set) the wbio chain; rbio is borrowed. bio_update_fn is application code called at connect/disconnect only, with no Rust reference held.

The BIOs a request context drives may be application-defined. They must not re-enter an operation on the same rctx during nbio; the state machine holds an exclusive Rust reference across every BIO call.

ERR_STATE slot buffers are owned by the state only when ERR_TXT_MALLOCED is set; borrowed slot data must remain valid until the entry is cleared or replaced. Allocations record NULL/0; releases record the err_local.h/err.c site.

ERR_print_errors_cb copies each entry into a local buffer before invoking the application callback, so the callback may raise errors; the remaining queue entries are left in place when it returns <= 0.

RSA keydata is owned by the keymgmt dispatch caller; import/export copy or borrow caller BIGNUMs according to selection, and the export callback borrows the parameter array only for the duration of the call.
EVP_PKEY_ASN1_METHOD objects are caller-owned and must outlive the registry and every lookup that borrows them. Registration takes no reference and there is no unregister API, matching the authority.

boundaries.mechanism: OSSL_HTTP_REQ_CTX construction, buffer/string ownership and free
residuals: wbio is owned only when free_wbio is set; rbio is always borrowed, as in the authority. A caller-provided wbio is not released by OSSL_HTTP_REQ_CTX_free.
proxy/server/port/expected_ct are CRYPTO_strdup copies released at the authority's own lines; redirection_url is a borrow into buf and is never released by free.

boundaries.mechanism: non-blocking request/response state machine over caller-driven BIOs
residuals: The state machine holds &mut OsslHttpReqCtx across BIO_read/BIO_write/BIO_gets/BIO_ctrl. A custom BIO method that re-enters any operation on the same rctx would form a second exclusive reference; its # Safety contract now excludes that re-entry.
buf is allocated for buf_size and BIO_gets is always called with exactly buf_size; the authority's 'line fills the buffer' and max-header-line refusals are retained before the in-place parse.
len_to_send/resp_len are bounded by the authority's checks and checked length helper, not by an arithmetic assertion.

boundaries.mechanism: connect/disconnect callback ownership, redirection loop and response BIO up-ref
residuals: bio_update_fn is invoked with no Rust reference to rctx (open, before the context exists; close, through a raw field). It may free or replace the connection BIO, and the returned BIO becomes the context's wbio exactly as in the authority.
On a callback refusal the supplied/caller-owned BIO is not freed; only a helper-created BIO chain is released.
OSSL_HTTP_get owns each redirection URL before assigning it to current_url and frees host/port/path at the authority's sites; a same-server redirect reuses the live host/port.
A response BIO is up-ref'd before being returned when the context is still alive (authority parity).

boundaries.mechanism: builder allocation/teardown, definition ownership and the push windows
residuals: The Vec body behind the authority's stack pointer is Rust-owned storage; its growth is invisible to CRYPTO_set_mem_functions and aborts on OOM rather than returning the authority's push failure. Total allocation parity is not claimed.
A push whose recorded size exceeds the eight-byte scalar recorder remains registered and later zero-fills, exactly as the authority leaves it.
Keys and value pointers are borrowed; the caller must keep them alive until to_param, and to_param empties the builder.

boundaries.mechanism: ordinary/secure block sizing, conversion pointer arithmetic and secure-block attachment
residuals: Block counts are now checked at push and re-checked in to_param; the conversion advances by alloc_blocks * OSSL_PARAM_ALIGN_SIZE under that invariant. An unrepresentable extent is a refused push.
The UTF-8 terminator extent is size + 1; an unrepresentable size is refused rather than wrapping as the authority's size_t addition does (deliberate safety divergence, recorded).
A secure block failures raise PARAM_BUILD_471; the ordinary allocation failure releases the secure block and returns NULL without raising, matching the authority.
Parameter values pushed from the secure heap are SECRET_DATA and are laid out only in the secure block; the returned array's terminator carries the secure block for OSSL_PARAM_free.

boundaries.mechanism: ERR_STATE block ownership, thread-local/shared state access and save/restore
residuals: The thread-local state has no destructor, exactly as before; only OSSL_ERR_STATE_new blocks are owned by OwnedErrState.
with_state reaches the shared per-thread state through dso_shared::err_state_ptr, so both DSOs observe one queue in the authority binding.

OSSL_ERR_STATE_save/save_to_mark/restore require a caller-owned state from OSSL_ERR_STATE_new; passing the thread's own state would alias, and the authority contracts likewise describe a preallocated separate state.
Error-queue text is PUBLIC_DATA metadata and is not cleansed; the authority does not cleanse it either.

boundaries.mechanism: slot ownership, data replacement/clearing and error reads
residuals: A returned file/func/data pointer remains owned by the ring slot and is valid only until the next ERR operation reuses or clears that slot (authority parity).
ERR_set_error_data takes ownership of a MALLOCED pointer and requires a whole seam block; without the flag the pointer is borrowed until the entry is cleared or replaced.
The ERR_add_error_txt length-bounded split at ERR_PRINT_BUF_SIZE - 100 is still not implemented (pre-existing recorded obligation).
ERR_error_string(NULL) writes a process-global 256-byte static buffer; the authority documents the function as not thread-safe, and the unsafe extern contract carries that obligation.

boundaries.mechanism: print callback and allocator-hook reentrancy edges
residuals: ERR_print_errors_cb copies an entry and releases the state reference before calling the application callback, so the callback may raise errors; there is no lock or &mut across it.

with_state allocates and releases inside its &mut closure, so the installed CRYPTO_set_mem_functions hooks run with that reference live. A hook that re-enters the ERR API on the same thread is now stated as outside the contract; the authority has the same hazard.
ERR_set_debug duplicates caller strings so a provider can unload while an error is queued.

boundaries.mechanism: RSA/RSA-PSS object path, import/export and get_params ownership
residuals: Keydata is owned by the keymgmt dispatch caller; this unit never releases it except through rsa_freedata.
rsa_export builds one builder array, passes it to the application callback for the call only, then frees it and the builder on every arm.
Imported private-key parameters are SECRET_DATA. They stay in the caller's BIGNUMs and in the key object; the provider does not copy them into a second ordinary-memory buffer.
common_load detaches the reference slot only after the sub-type check passes; a caller must provide an aligned slot and a live Rsa.

boundaries.mechanism: generation context allocation, set_params, progress callback and cleanup
residuals: gen_init's failure path releases pub_exp with BN_free at the authority's line and the block with CRYPTO_free; rsa_gen_cleanup uses BN_clear_free for the same member, matching the two authority sites.
rsa_gencb invokes the application callback with parameters that point into its own frame; no lock or Rust reference is held across it. The callback may re-enter keymgmt.
The FIPS ACVP members are absent on this profile, as documented.
A reference of the wrong size is refused without dereferencing; a matching reference is read as a pointer-aligned *mut Rsa slot and is detached in place.
rsa_dup requires the keypair selection bit and delegates to ossl_rsa_dup.
The registry is now serialised by one non-reentrant mutex; the slot and every stack read/mutation run under it, so concurrent add/lookup is no longer a Rust data race.
A registry operation that raises an error allocates through the CRYPTO seam under the lock; an allocator hook that re-enters the registry would deadlock (authority-parity liveness, no UB).
The registry stores borrowed method pointers and has no unregister API; a caller that frees a registered DYNAMIC method leaves a dangling entry (authority parity, now stated in add0's contract).
EVP_PKEY_asn1_new's two CRYPTO_strdup blocks and the zalloc block are released by the authority's three free lines; a failed second duplicate drops the first through the same destructor.
EVP_PKEY_asn1_copy copies only the function-pointer body and restores the five identity/ownership members, including the self-copy case.
EVP_PKEY_asn1_free ignores a non-DYNAMIC method, so the standard static objects survive a call.

boundaries.mechanism: find/find_str/alias walk and exported callback tables
residuals: find_str takes one registry snapshot per call, so its count and per-index reads agree even while another thread registers; method pointers themselves are borrowed, caller-owned objects.
An alias cycle is an infinite loop, as in the authority; the engine arms are absent on this profile and are recorded rather than stubbed.
The standard method array and the two dispatch tables are immutable statics; the Sync marker on EvpPkeyAsn1Method covers only those compile-time objects.

defects.class: unchecked allocation/offset arithmetic (size + 1, blocks * align, array and block sums)
defects.description: param_push stored ossl_param_bytes_to_blocks(alloc) and added it to total_blocks/secure_blocks unchecked; to_param computed (1 + num) * sizeof(OSSL_PARAM), p_blks + total_blocks and align * blocks unchecked; push_utf8_string computed size + 1 unchecked. An extreme caller-asserted size could wrap, under-allocate, and then make param_bld_convert write pd.size bytes past the block.
defects.fix: push_utf8_string uses checked_add; param_push rejects a block extent whose align multiplication overflows and uses checked_add for both counters; to_param uses checked_add/checked_mul for the array size, block sum and secure size and fails before any allocation. The conversion still advances under the now-established invariant.
defects.regression: New control params::build::tests::unrepresentable_value_extent_is_refused_at_push. Negative control observed: disabling the param_push check makes it fail with left 1 / right 0; the check was restored and the test passes.

defects.class: allocator-seam coordinate (bare file path and line 0 at every site)
defects.description: param_build.c is a plain .c, so the admitted build's __FILE__ is ../../src/openssl-3.6.4/crypto/param_build.c; the seam recorded crypto/param_build.c and line 0 for all allocations and releases. The authority's zalloc/free/malloc/secure sites are lines 55, 68, 93, 110, 119, 469, 475 and 477.
defects.fix: FILE now carries the source-tree prefix and each seam call uses its own site constant. The three definition windows distinguish the failed-push release (68) from free_all_params (110).
defects.regression: params::build tests and the full suite; no allocator-transcript court targets this unit (authority differential NOT_RUN).

defects.class: allocator-seam size (builder block 40 bytes instead of the authority's 24)
defects.description: The Vec was stored inline, so CRYPTO_zalloc(size_of::<OSSL_PARAM_BLD>()) requested 40 bytes where the authority requests two size_t plus a stack pointer (24). A caller-installed allocator hook observed the wrong num.
defects.fix: The builder is #[repr(C)] with total_blocks, secure_blocks and a pointer to a Rust-owned ParamDefs body; the block is 24 bytes, the Vec lives behind the pointer, and free reconstructs the Box before releasing the block.

defects.description: http_client.c is a plain .c, so the authority's allocator hook sees ../../src/openssl-3.6.4/crypto/http/http_client.c; the seam recorded crypto/http/http_client.c on every OwnedBuf allocation/release. The error-raise sites already used the prefixed path.
defects.fix: FILE now carries the source-tree prefix; all allocation/release line numbers were already the authority's own.
defects.regression: Full suite; no allocator-transcript court targets this unit (authority differential NOT_RUN).

defects.class: allocator-seam coordinate (releases recorded NULL/0 instead of err_local.h/err.c)
defects.description: ERR allocations deliberately record NULL/0, but releases are asymmetric: err_clear_data/err_set_data/err_set_debug/err_clear free through OPENSSL_free at err_local.h:25/79/56/66/92/94, and OSSL_ERR_STATE_free frees the block at err.c:209. The crate recorded NULL/0 for every release.
defects.fix: Added ERR_LOCAL_FILE/ERR_C_FILE and the six release-line constants and used them in clear_data, set_data, set_debug, clear and OwnedErrState::drop; the module comment now states the allocation/release asymmetry.
defects.regression: runtime::err 14/0 and the full suite; no allocator-transcript court targets the error queue (authority differential NOT_RUN).

defects.description: ErrState is a #[repr(C)] record of raw pointers and mutable per-thread fields, yet it carried unsafe impl Sync with a comment saying the marker was required by thread_local!. thread_local! needs only 'static, and UnsafeCell<ErrState> is !Sync regardless, so the claim was unnecessary and falsely advertised cross-thread sharing.
defects.fix: Removed the unsafe impl and replaced the comment with the correct per-thread/!Sync rationale. The crate compiles and the full suite passes without it.

defects.class: data race / UB on the process-global application ASN.1 method registry
defects.description: app_methods was a static mut pointer read and mutated by add0, get_count, get0 and pkey_asn1_find with no synchronisation. Concurrent registration and lookup (or two registrations) is a Rust data race on the pointer and on the stack's Vec, and therefore UB; the authority has the same unsynchronised shape.
defects.fix: The slot and every stack read/mutation now go through one std::sync::Mutex<AppMethods>; a locked helper serves get_count/get0/pkey_asn1_find/find_str, and add0 holds the same lock for create/find/push/sort. No application callback runs under the lock.
defects.regression: evp::pkey_asn1 tests and the full suite. A Loom/TSan control for the concurrent case is NOT_RUN.

defects.class: narrowing-cast parity defect in the RSA bits floor check
defects.description: The floor check cast size_t nbits to c_int before comparing with RSA_MIN_MODULUS_BITS. The authority compares size_t against the int constant (promoted to size_t), so values >= 2^31 passed set_params in the authority but were rejected here.
defects.fix: Compared (*gctx).nbits with RSA_MIN_MODULUS_BITS as usize, preserving the authority's size_t comparison. The later (int) cast into RSA_generate_multi_prime_key is unchanged and still matches the authority.
defects.regression: Full suite; rsa_kmgmt has no unit test, so an authority differential for the >= 2^31 window is NOT_RUN.

defects.description: common_load reads and writes through *const *mut Rsa / *mut *mut Rsa, which requires pointer alignment and a non-NULL reference when the size matches; its # Safety stated only the readable extent.
defects.fix: The contract now requires non-NULL and suitable alignment for a *mut Rsa when reference_sz matches, and a live slot this call may clear.
defects.regression: Contract review; no runtime control for a misaligned reference exists (NOT_RUN).

defects.class: unchecked string-size sums feeding slot allocations
defects.description: attach_message, openssl_rs_err_set_error, openssl_rs_err_add_data and ERR_add_error_txt computed len + 1, old_len + add_len and old_len + sep_len + txt_len unchecked. A wrapped extent would under-allocate and then be copied into.
defects.fix: Each sum now uses checked_add and treats an unrepresentable extent like a refused allocation (no data attached).
defects.regression: runtime::err tests and the full suite; the arms require unrepresentable input and have no runtime canary (NOT_RUN).

defects.description: OSSL_HTTP_REQ_CTX_nbio holds &mut OsslHttpReqCtx across every BIO operation, but the # Safety contract did not exclude a custom BIO method re-entering the same rctx.
defects.fix: The contract now states that a custom BIO reached through mem/wbio/rbio must not re-enter an operation on the same rctx during the call.
defects.regression: Contract review; no custom-BIO reentrancy canary exists (NOT_RUN).

defects.description: EVP_PKEY_asn1_add0's contract required only a live method that outlives the registry; it did not state that releasing a registered DYNAMIC method leaves a dangling entry (there is no unregister API).
defects.fix: The contract now records the borrowed-lifetime/dangling-entry obligation, matching the authority.

focused_tests: params::build:: 2 passed / 0 failed (size parity and checked-extent control)
runtime::err (filter runtime::err covers err + err_state) 14 passed / 0 failed

probes: No affected OPENSSL_RS_ADV_PROBE arm exists for these five units.
batch.negative_control: Disabling the param_push extent check made params::build::tests::unrepresentable_value_extent_is_refused_at_push fail with left 1 / right 0; the check was restored and the test passes.

not_run: ASan / Miri / Loom / TSan for the five audited units
a concurrent-registry control for B10-D7 (the Mutex is the repair; no Loom/TSan run)
allocator-transcript/authority differentials for the params builder, HTTP client, error queue and RSA keymgmt
custom-BIO reentrancy and allocator-hook reentrancy canaries

discharged: B10-D2/D4/D5 allocator-seam file and line coordinates
retained: A custom BIO method must not re-enter the same HTTP request context during nbio (now stated).
An allocator hook must not re-enter the ERR API from inside with_state's allocation/release windows (now stated; authority-parity hazard).
An allocator hook that re-enters the ASN.1 registry while it is locked would deadlock (liveness, authority parity).
Registered EVP_PKEY_ASN1_METHOD pointers are borrowed and caller-owned; no unregister API exists.
Builder keys and value pointers are borrowed until to_param; the Vec body is Rust-owned and invisible to the CRYPTO hook.
Returned error-queue string pointers are slot-owned and valid only until the next operation on that slot.

graduation.note: No consumer family graduates. No safe Rust caller can reach UB through these modules: every exported entry is unsafe with a stated C contract, and the one safe-internal global (the ASN.1 registry) is now mutex-serialised. The retained callback/allocator-hook obligations are stated at the boundary.
